title: Is There Enough Item Variance in Safety Benchmarks for IRT to Work?

original_idea.body:
# Is There Enough Item Variance in Safety Benchmarks for IRT to Work? An Empirical Check

**Problem:** Apply IRT to AI safety benchmarks

**Direction:** For several safety benchmarks, compute the empirical distribution of item pass rates (proportion of models that refuse/comply) across items. Test whether item difficulty spans the full range needed to discriminate models at different safety ability levels, whether item variance exceeds a minimum threshold (e.g., items with p > 0.95 or p < 0.05 carry near-zero information), and how many items remain informative after removing floor/ceiling items.

**Why it matters:** If safety benchmarks consist mostly of items that all advanced models pass (refuse harmful requests) or all models fail (comply with jailbreaks), there is minimal item variance and IRT has little to work with. This is a prerequisite diagnostic—if variance is too low, the benchmark cannot differentiate safety ability levels and needs more items in the middle difficulty range.

**Relevant context:** MMLU reached saturation by mid-2024 when top models scored above 85%, losing discriminative power. Safety benchmarks may face the same problem in reverse—if all frontier models achieve >95% refusal rates on standard prompts, there is ceiling-level variance that IRT cannot leverage. tinyBenchmarks explicitly used IRT to select high-information items.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Vague impact. This is a diagnostic feasibility check for IRT applicability. It does not directly reduce risk; it determines whether a methodology is viable. Impact requires subsequent work.

low_compute.reasoning: Computing pass rate distributions from existing data. Minimal compute, basic descriptive statistics.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Computing proportions and pass rate distributions is basic descriptive statistics accessible to beginners. No advanced methods required.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: compute pass rate distributions for a few benchmarks, count floor/ceiling items. A single descriptive analysis with clear numeric output.

quick_reasoning: Directly addresses a prerequisite feasibility question for IRT on safety benchmarks with concrete variance diagnostics; safety relevance is clear as a foundational check.
